name: Nympha
overview: Nympha was a female believer in the early Christian church known for hosting a church meeting in her house in Colossae. While her tribal affiliation is not recorded, her role as a host of a local church gathering highlights her significance in the early Christian community. There is a possibility that her name is related to the masculine form Nymphas, but the Scripture specifically mentions her as Nympha.
namesAndTitles: The name Nympha appears once in Scripture without a specific meaning provided. It is presented simply as a proper name, with no indication that it was given by God or holds a particular symbolic significance.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record any family relationships for Nympha beyond her unique role of having a church in her house. There are no other relationships mentioned in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Nympha's significance lies in her provision of a meeting place for the church in Colossae, demonstrating the early Christian practice of gathering in homes for worship and fellowship. This detail underscores the active participation of women in the life of the early church and the importance of hospitality in supporting the spread of the gospel. Though little else is known about her, Nympha's mention affirms the vital role of lay believers in the establishment and nurturing of Christian communities.
